title: What to watch at the open
text: The market is closed right now, so prices below are still from Monday's close. Stocks jumped on Monday: SPY rose 2.4% and QQQ rose 3.5%. Today, watch two things. First, a government inflation report on consumer prices comes out at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, before the market opens. Second, see whether the chip makers that bounced hard on Monday can hold their gains. One big up day does not tell us what comes next.

title: Inflation report lands before the open
text: Inflation means prices for everyday things are rising. The government releases a report on it today at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. If prices rose more than people expected, interest rates may stay high, and that can hurt fast growing tech companies. If prices rose less than expected, stocks may like it. The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, the highest in the last 12 months, so this report matters.

title: NVIDIA reports its results on November 17
text: NVIDIA fell 4.3% on Monday to $178.67 while the other four AI supplier companies rose. It is still about 27% below its 52 week high of $243.37. The company says it will share its quarterly results on November 17 after the market closes. Earnings days can move a stock a lot in either direction, so it is a date worth marking.

title: Big bounces can reverse fast
text: AMD rose 13.3%, Vertiv rose 9.6% and Broadcom rose 8.8% on Monday, and Rocket Lab rose 10.9%. These companies have high betas (1.5 to 2.6), which means they swing much more than the market. Their risk scores run from 5.8 to 10 out of 10. After a jump like this, a pullback is just as possible as more gains.

title: Lesson 44: What is an earnings report?
text: Four times a year, public companies share a report card called an earnings report. It tells us how much they sold, how much profit they made, and what they expect next. Investors do not only look at whether the numbers were good. They compare them to what experts guessed beforehand. A company can make record profits and still see its stock drop if people hoped for even more. That is why prices can jump or fall fast on earnings day. NVIDIA's report on November 17 is a good example to follow along with.
